chunks: From him, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abi 'Ubaydah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام: regarding

A man upon whom a hadd punishment had become obligatory, but he was not punished until he became mentally disturbed. He said: “If he had made the hadd binding upon himself while he was sound, with no affliction of loss of intellect, the hadd is to be carried out upon him, whatever it may be.”

key_terms.أَوْجَبَ: made obligatory or established as due
key_terms.أُقِيمَ: it is to be carried out or enforced
key_terms.خُولِطَ: he became mentally disturbed or confused in intellect

ai.seo_question: Is a hadd punishment still carried out if the offender later loses mental soundness?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person who became liable to a hadd punishment while mentally sound, but whose punishment was delayed until after he lost mental clarity. Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام states that if the liability was established while the person was of sound mind, the hadd punishment is still to be carried out.
